nodes.detailed_figure_description: Hand-drawn voltage-versus-time graph. The vertical axis is labeled V, with dashed horizontal guides at +V₀ and −V₀. A sinusoidal waveform oscillates about the horizontal t(s) axis. An orange bracket beneath the graph marks the interval labeled “1 cycle.”
nodes.figure_alternative: Sinusoidal voltage waveform ranging from +V₀ to −V₀ over time, with one cycle marked.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: V equals V naught sine of omega t.

nodes.figure_alternative: Hand-drawn series circuit containing a resistor, capacitor, and circular AC voltage-source symbol. An arrow identifies the circular sine-wave symbol with the text “circuit symbol for AC voltage source.”

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: Sixty cycles per second times two pi radians per cycle equals three hundred seventy-seven radians per second.
V R M S equals the square root of the average of V squared.

nodes.text: FACT: the average value of sin² θ (or cos² θ) over a cycle is 1/2.

nodes.detailed_figure_description: Hand-drawn graph with vertical axis y and horizontal axis t. The y-axis has a mark at 1. A repeating rounded waveform begins at zero, rises to approximately 1, returns to the axis, and repeats; portions dip slightly below the axis. The curve is labeled “Sin(ωt).”
nodes.figure_alternative: Repeating waveform labeled Sin(ωt), plotted against time with a marked amplitude of 1.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: The average of sine squared of omega t equals one half.

V R M S equals the square root of the average of V naught squared sine squared of omega t, which equals the square root of V naught squared times one half, which equals V naught divided by the square root of two.
V R M S equals V naught divided by the square root of two.

warnings.message: The graph is labeled “Sin(ωt),” but its predominantly nonnegative repeating shape and the surrounding discussion concern sin²(ωt); the visible label may be missing a superscript 2. The slight dips below zero are preserved in the description.
